mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome—I'm so glad you're here with me. Imagine a world where injustice isn’t just in the news, but woven into the fabric of everyday life. Now, picture what it takes not just to survive, but to raise your voice, and insist on dignity when everything around you says to stay silent. That’s the journey we’ll share together, as we step into the story of Patrisse Khan-Cullors—whose life and activism as co-founder of the Black Lives Matter movement have inspired millions. Through her eyes, we’ll witness how growing up Black in America means facing poverty, police brutality, and the constant risk of being misunderstood. But you’ll also discover the fierce love, unbreakable family ties, and deep community roots that fuel the fight for justice. When They Call You a Terrorist: A Black Lives Matter Memoir, written by Patrisse Khan-Cullors, invites us to look past the headlines and hashtags, and truly see the people behind the movement. Together, we’ll explore how personal pain can spark collective action, and how vulnerability and courage walk hand in hand. We’ll reflect on what it means to belong, to be valued, and to speak truth when the world would rather you stay quiet. So, let’s begin this journey, side by side. We’ll find hope, solidarity, and the unwavering belief that a better future really is possible—if we dare to imagine it, and work for it, together.
